solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink six-pack in hotel in centre of Ostend

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined stomach muscles, or abs
taken as written

indicators.note: the hotel letter is put inside the following letters
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the middle two of a six-letter word

parts.note: the Belgian port supplies its central pair of letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: put a six-pack of something into a hotel bar in the middle of a Belgian port town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is just the word itself, and the second is the signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, a classic example of a drink.

clue.text: Ordering lamb and sheep is utter profanity

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges the combined animal words

explanation.surface: A diner ordering both lamb and mutton in one meal is somehow committing an outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak irreverently of sacred things, which is uttering profanity as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Force that is constraining politician on Left

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes first, so the left letter follows
the 'that is' letters hold the politician within them

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A force restraining a left-wing politician, like a party whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them, a synonym of force as a verb.

clue.text: Health worker discovered ether subdues sex attacker

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting over something is to subdue it, so these letters come first
dis-covered: the word ether loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: its inner letters are kept
a rapist is a sexual attacker

explanation.surface: A news story: a doctor finds that anaesthetic ether can knock out an assailant.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients physically or psychologically, so is a type of healthcare professional.

clue.text: Persuaded wayward niece to cross Thailand with diamonds

indicators.note: the diamonds letter is added at the end
the rearranged niece goes across, around, the letter for Thailand
a wayward relative goes astray, so the letters of niece are rearranged

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration for Thailand

explanation.surface: Someone talked a wayward niece into smuggling diamonds over the Thai border.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed means lured or tempted into doing something, a close synonym of persuaded.

clue.text: Berate wife and mother about makeshift dwelling

parts.note: to wig is an old word meaning to scold or rebuke

indicators.note: turned about, the word for mother is read backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Telling off your wife and mother about the shabby shack they live in.
explanation.walkthrough: To WIG (as in 'wigging', a scolding) means to berate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a dome-shaped hut of poles and bark or hides, a simple temporary shelter.

clue.text: Picked up cetacean's mournful cries

indicators.note: heard, as if picked up on a radio, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: whales are cetaceans; read here as the plural whales

explanation.surface: Hydrophones picked up the haunting song of a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Wails are long high-pitched cries of grief or pain, so mournful cries in plain terms.

clue.text: Exalted German nobleman embracing setter? That's disgusting!

indicators.note: the nobleman's letters wrap around the following pieces

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
the setter refers to themself as I
fie is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A haughty German aristocrat clutches the crossword setter, who protests in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorified means praised or elevated in status, as exalted does.

clue.text: Missing penultimate letter, publication's void

indicators.note: the publication's second-to-last letter is dropped

parts.note: an annual is a yearly publication; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A rule about a printed document: if it lacks a letter near the end, it is invalid.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare invalid, which is to void a contract or marriage, both as verbs.

clue.text: Cross-section of society with more than enough

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A pollster boasts of a representative slice of society, and plenty of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a representative selection, which is what a cross-section of a population is.

clue.text: Model ragged Eric about old navy hat

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes round the next letters
made ragged, the letters of Eric are mixed up

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A scruffy model called Eric poses in an antique naval hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorne is a three-cornered cocked hat, worn by eighteenth-century naval officers.

clue.text: Devices initially planted inside baroque palace in Sweden

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the jumbled letters
baroque means extravagantly ornate or irregular, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder with in

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Gadgets have been planted inside an ornate Swedish palace, perhaps bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'palace in' together, so 'in' is fodder rather than an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliances are machines or gadgets designed for a particular task, so devices in general.

clue.text: Work-shy revolutionary withheld important parts

indicators.note: revolving the letters means reading them backwards
the letters are taken from parts of the two words, across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of withheld and the start of important

explanation.surface: A rebel kept back the vital components of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like it signals pieces put together, but here it marks letters lying within the clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means lazy and avoiding work, which is what work-shy describes.

clue.text: Sign termination of lease on Golf car

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter is used
the Mini is a classic British small car

explanation.surface: Signing to end the lease on a Volkswagen Golf car.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf seems to be the VW car, but it is G from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: The same archetypal, grasping knight with nervous mannerism

indicators.note: the ideal letters hold the following pieces

parts.note: ideal means a perfect or archetypal example
N is the chess notation for knight
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Every classic knight in the story has the same nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike in every detail, so it is the same thing.

clue.text: Heartless Greek character born on island is prisoner

indicators.note: the born letters are placed after the island
without its heart, the middle letter of the Greek letter is removed

parts.note: delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet
née introduces a woman's birth name

explanation.surface: A cruel Greek man born on an island is now behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is someone held in custody, which is a prisoner.

clue.text: Vandal, say, damaged brainstem

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vandal has caused damage to someone's brain stem.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, a Vandal is a member of the Germanic people who sacked Rome; 'say' marks him as an example of a tribe member.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vandals were a Germanic tribe, so a Vandal is one example of a member of a tribe.

clue.text: Lower boom at sea to make space

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor lowers the boom on a yacht to make room on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough room to move freely, an idiom for adequate space.

clue.text: One who chooses district occupied by the French

indicators.note: the district letters hold the French article inside

parts.note: a sector is a district or area
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A wartime district occupied by French forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks people or things, such as players for a national team.

clue.text: Leaves on small spacecraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: rocket is a salad leaf, called arugula in America

explanation.surface: Someone departs aboard a little spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' seems to be a verb of departing, but it is the salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets are vehicles propelled into space, so spacecraft in the plural sense.

clue.text: Fashionable young lady gets back from Egypt owing money

parts.note: in means trendy, in fashion
a deb is a debutante, a young upper-class woman entering society

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A stylish debutante returns from an Egyptian holiday with big bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in debt means owing money to a creditor.

clue.text: Fatuous paper written by attorney

indicators.note: the paper is written after the attorney

parts.note: DA is a district attorney
FT is the Financial Times, the paper hosting this puzzle

explanation.surface: A silly article written in the pink paper by a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft means silly or foolish, a close synonym of fatuous.

clue.text: Silver and gold originally adorned market place

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: An ancient market square decorated in silver and gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square and marketplace of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: A group of sailors welcoming D Company aboard ship? They can't be criticised!

indicators.note: being aboard the ship means inside its letters

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: the crew takes the letters in

parts.note: a crew is the group of sailors on a ship

explanation.surface: A ship's crew welcome a military company on board, and nobody dares criticise them.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the literal letter, from D Company as in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred cows are ideas or institutions treated as above criticism, an idiom from the holy cattle of Hinduism.

clue.text: Young rustic women essentially engaged in wrongdoing

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for wrongdoing

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: its middle letter is used

explanation.surface: A young country lad and some women are caught up in misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' reads as one insertion phrase, but 'engaged' only supplies its central letter, and 'in' alone does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a country youth in pastoral poetry, often a shepherd lover.

clue.text: Actors given voice class

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors are given speaking parts in a classy production.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social group, as in the Hindu system, so a social class.

clue.text: Caught on toilet in church meeting

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

indicators.note: the toilet letters go inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone caught on the loo during a church meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclave is a private assembly, most famously the cardinals' gathering to elect a pope.

clue.text: A Celt put on minute talisman

indicators.note: the following pieces are put after the minute letter

parts.note: Scots are one of the Celtic peoples

explanation.surface: A Celtic warrior wears a tiny lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good luck, like a lucky charm.

clue.text: Measure barring English from ship

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so the English letter is taken out

parts.note: a galleon is a large sailing ship

explanation.surface: A rule to prevent English sailors from boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of liquid volume, so a measure.

clue.text: Boy on radio supports renewable energy suppliers

indicators.note: heard on the radio, so a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a son is a boy
beams are structural supports

explanation.surface: A radio presenter's son backs solar power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbeams carry the sun's light, the source of solar power, a renewable energy.
